title: Business Office Standard — Payment-Plan Charges and the Absorption of a Credit, Patient Financial Account
content:
**Standard.** Which open charges of the Patient Financial Account absorb a credit before it is refunded depends on the patient's payment plan under Patient Payment Plans:

- when the patient has an active payment plan with an installment paid in the six calendar months before the handling date and no missed installment recorded in those six months, the charges that plan carries do not absorb the credit, and the plan's remaining balance is added back to the credit;
- when the patient has a delinquent payment plan with a missed installment recorded in those six months, those charges absorb only the missed installments, and the plan's remaining balance less the missed installment amounts of those six months is added back;
- otherwise no different absorption applies under this standard.

**Records read.** The plan's status (active or delinquent) and remaining balance, and the plan's ledger entries of installments paid and installments missed with their dates and amounts.

**Six calendar months.** A window of calendar months for the credit refund ends on the handling date and reaches back that many months, a date on the same calendar day that many months earlier falling outside it.

## Determinations

| Plan status | Installment paid within 6 months | Missed installment within 6 months | Added back to the credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| active | yes | no | the plan's remaining balance |
| active | yes or no | yes | nothing under this standard |
| active | no | no | nothing under this standard |
| delinquent | — | yes | remaining balance less the missed installment amounts |
| delinquent | — | no | nothing under this standard |

**Hypothetical figures.** A credit balance of 90.00 on an account whose patient has an active plan with 420.00 remaining, an installment paid last month and nothing missed: 90.00 plus 420.00 gives 510.00 before any amount kept. A delinquent plan with 420.00 remaining and two missed installments of 70.00 each in the six months: 420.00 less 140.00 is 280.00 added back, giving 370.00.
